newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Premier sees IMF tranches released soon.
newsitem.headline: Russian Premier sees IMF tranches released soon.

text.p: MOSCOW, January 27 - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Monday he expected the International Monetary Fund to release tranches of a $10 billion three-year loan delayed from November and December in the next few days, Interfax news agency said.
"This business (of delays) will be finished and the tranches will be received," Chernomyrdin said.
Chernomyrdin said Russia was back on track regarding IMF economic targets after problems late last year, especially with tax collection.
Each tranche is worth about $340 million.
"In November and December we were on schedule," he said. "Monthly macroeconomic indicators are under control."

First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin told RIA news agency that talks with the IMF on a programme for 1997 were almost finished and that all conditions for receiving the delayed tranches would be in place in a few days.
